description: Contradicts ARC_TEMPLATES on purpose (see template_disagreements). Every ARC_TEMPLATES arc (crisis_recovery, exec_sponsor_change, competitive_displacement, ...) assumes a relationship-event-precedes-disengagement direction and routes every signal chain through a decision/intervention step before any outcome. This world reverses the first assumption on one edge, omits an edge a technical-escalation-style template prior would expect, and adds a real edge no template contains at all. AT-1 requires: discovery run against this world's output must recover THIS world's schema, not the templates'.

dag.note: REVERSED vs ARC_TEMPLATES.exec_sponsor_change (which asserts champion_change -> engagement_gap, i.e. departure causes the gap). Here disengagement precedes and causes the departure, not the other way around.

REAL EDGE NO TEMPLATE CONTAINS. Every ARC_TEMPLATES arc only connects a risk-signal chain to at_risk/protected outcomes, never to an expansion outcome. Here a thermal/power constraint drives a real expansion interest (racing to lock in priority allocation before a capacity crunch) -- a risk-to-expansion link no template models at all.

Gives interconnect_bottleneck its own independent downstream effect, distinct from reliability_sla_breach's (e7) -- makes the no_relationship absence below between the two actually testable: both types now occur for the same account with no edge connecting THEM to each other, rather than neither type ever being generated at all.

template_disagreements.template_edge: signal:2 -> signal:3 (champion departure led to engagement gap)
signal:3 -> signal:4 (technical signal escalates to critical incident)
template_disagreements.this_world: no edge between these two types at all in this world's true DAG -- see no_relationship absence below

template_disagreements.template: (none -- no ARC_TEMPLATES arc connects a risk-chain signal to an expansion outcome)

absences.note: Real and admitted at this world's window (30d) -- included as a control that this pair is NOT beyond-lag here, contrast with world_a's genuinely-excluded case. See eval_profile/event_engine.py: only pairs whose true_lag exceeds admission_lag_window_days are actually scored as beyond_lag_window; this entry documents the boundary case.

account_archetypes.note: interconnect_bottleneck and reliability_sla_breach both occur for these accounts, each with its own independent downstream effect, no edge between the two -- the account population the no_relationship absence (interconnect_bottleneck, reliability_sla_breach) is actually testable against.

revenue_model.note: Same bound as world_a -- the platform invariant (AT-8), not a per-world choice.
